subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept this internal async/yielding bootstrap-context change as the narrow fix for the linked embedded_run stall despite compatibility-sensitive bootstrap context and scheduling behavior?
rationale: The diff has no concrete correctness blocker, but repository policy treats bootstrap context, session state, plugin hooks, and runtime scheduling as maintainer-owned merge-risk surfaces that tests alone do not settle.

options.title: Accept focused bootstrap fix
options.body: Merge after exact-head gates if maintainers accept the focused terminal proof and internal scheduling behavior as the right narrow mitigation.

options.title: Require connected run proof
options.body: Hold until a live embedded_run channel or keepalive scenario proves message delivery remains responsive under bootstrap load.

options.title: Defer to broader architecture
options.body: Pause or close this branch if maintainers want worker isolation or priority scheduling to own this event-loop bottleneck instead.

recommendation.title: Accept focused bootstrap fix
recommendation.body: Merge after exact-head gates if maintainers accept the focused terminal proof and internal scheduling behavior as the right narrow mitigation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history evidence for the internal hook and bootstrap hook architecture points to this routing candidate.
